ratings_why.fun: Over a 7 because Borrow turns every slot into a combo question: a Jack left of Longshanks boxes twice, a Leveret behind Moon-Gazer is a free turner, the Witch steals the enemy's text, and Moon-Caller can flip the whole board to Full mid-fight.
ratings_why.distinct: A moon you wind separately for the shop and for the fight is fresh, but copy-text and day/night clocks are familiar ideas from other games.

verdict_why: The core is ready; one rules gap (borrowed sell and self-naming text) needs a line before it can be read.

points.text: Borrow says borrowed When played text never fires, but says nothing on borrowed sell or death text. Does a Leveret or Jack borrowing Moon-Gazer, Old Wat or Moon-Caller turn the moon, and does a sold Jack borrowing Old Wat bring back a Jack or an Old Wat?

Leverets borrowing sell triggers is the best hidden combo here: Created 0-gold bodies that turn the moon when sold under Full. If kept, say so in the builds; if not wanted, rule it out in the Borrow text.
The Three Hares beside a Ribboned Jack that borrows a Full Moon payoff spreads that payoff three ways; worth a build line, since it is the cleanest Borrow-plus-multiplier knot in the tribe.
Waning is still a pass-through phase. A Waning card that rewards turning the moon past Full (e.g. gains per phase entered this turn) would give the clock build a reason to overshoot.
Meikle Care's tier note says she keeps Borrow on, but Waxing still sits between Fulls; either make that true (skip Waxing too, at a cost) or fix the note.

standouts.why: Cheapest card with the most combo reach: its value is whatever you place to its left, across every tribe.
Dying turns the board Moonlit mid-fight, switching on Bristle, Borrow and Full Moon payoffs as a surprise the opponent's scouting can't see.
Leveret growth plus positional lenders plus triples makes a capstone you build around for turns, and it forks against Meikle Care.

weakest.why: Plain gold on New Moon with no interaction beyond Waxwell doubling it.
A standard team-buff on Full; it does the expected thing and little else.
Fine for Leverets, but the only Waning card and a flat end-of-turn buffer otherwise.

flags.note: With Waxwell she fires twice a turn, and Created copies of a Tier 6 Hare reach triples fast; the back row's three slots are the main cap.
Always-on copy of another tribe's capstone from Tier 5.
When borrowed, 'get Old Wat back' is ambiguous: a new Old Wat, the borrower, or nothing.
